newsitem.title: USA: IMM marks, Swiss and yen close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM marks, Swiss and yen close slightly higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, with March marks, Swiss francs and yen all posting minor gains.
Traders said the dollar was taking a breather from its recent multi-year gains against the mark and yen, with month-end dollar profit-taking keeping spot under pressure.
"I think everything (in the dollar) is pretty positive still," one IMM trader said. "This profit-taking had to be expected.
Traders said action was light most of the day in the key currencies.
Traders said the market gleaned little direction from testimony to the Senate Finance Committee from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
"There wasn't really any significant movement in here today," a trading floor manager said. "It more or less looks like followthrough from comments made overnight," he said.

Overnight losses in dollar/yen had been tied to comments from senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara that suggested Japan will intervene in the foreign exchange market when the timing is effective.
Also overnight, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he expected the normalisation of the mark's exchange rate versus the dollar to end soon.
"I also think it's a matter of people squaring up a little before GDP tomorrow, but otherwise it was uneventful really," the trading floor manager said.
Fourth-quarter advance GDP will be released at 0730 CST/1330 GMT Friday and was forecast up 3.9 percent versus up 2.1 percent in the previous report.
Another trader said the market was "jockeying around" ahead of a hefty data line-up next week.
Also on tap next week is the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
The floor manager put March marks resistance for Friday at $0.6181, with support at $0.6080.
"I think if we get above $0.6150, we'll probably test that $0.6181 area," he said.

At settlement, March yen were were up $0.000025 at $0.008275, marks were up $0.0021 to $0.6130, Swiss francs were up $0.0009 at $0.7062, sterling was down $0.0072 at $1.6122, and the Canadian dollar was down $0.0011 at $0.7439.
